G6601:
αὐθήμερος [ἡμέρα]
I. made or done on the very day, Aeschin.
II. adv. αὐθημερόν (oxyt.), on the very day, on the same day, immediately, Aesch., etc.; ionic αὐτημερόν, Hdt.
G6603:
αὖλαξ
1. a furrow made in ploughing, Lat. sulcus, Hom., etc.; αὔλακ’ ἐλαύνειν to draw a furrow, Hes.
2. metaph. of a wife as the bearer of children, Soph., Eur.
3. metaph. also, a furrow in the skin, a gash, wound, Aesch., Eur.
4. = ὄγμος, a swathe, Theocr. (Prob. from same Root as ὁλκός, Lat. sulcus, from ἕλκω.）
G6605:
αὐλών [αὐλός]
1. a hollow way, defile, glen, Hhymn., Hdt., Ar.
2. a canal, aqueduct, trench, Hdt.
3. a channel, strait, Aesch.; αὐλῶνες πόντιοι the sea straits, i. e. the Archipelago, Soph.
G6606:
αὔρα [ἄημι]
1. air in motion, a breeze, esp. a cool breeze, the fresh air of morning, Lat. aura, Od., Hdt., attic Poets; rare in Prose:—metaph. steam, Ar.
2. metaph. also, of changeful events, Eur., Ar.; of anything thrilling, Eur.
G6608:
αὐτόθι
Adv. for αὐτοῦ, on the spot, Il., Hdt., attic
G6609:
αὐτομολέω [From αὐτόμολος]
to desert, Hdt., attic; αὐτ. πρὸς τοὺς Πέρσας Hdt.; ἐς Ἀθήνας ἐκ Περσέων id.
G6611:
αὐτόχθων
I. sprung from the land itself, Lat. terrigena: αὐτόχθονες, οἱ, like Lat. Indigenae, aborigines, natives, Hdt., Thuc.; of the Athenians, Eur., Ar., etc.
II. as adj. indigenous, Hdt.
G6612:
αὐχήν [Deriv. uncertain.]
I. the neck, throat, of men and beasts, Hom., etc.
II. metaph. any narrow passage, a neck of land, isthmus, Hdt., Xen.
2. a narrow sea, strait, Hdt., Aesch.; of the point at which the Danube spreads into several branches, Hdt.
3. a narrow mountain-pass, defile, id.
G6613:
αὐχμός [αὔω to burn]
1. drought, Hdt., Thuc.
2. the effects of drought, squalor, Plat.
G6614:
αὐχμώδης [εἶδος]
looking dry, squalid, κόμη Eur.: τὸ αὐχμῶδες drought, Hdt.
G6615:
ἀφαγνίζω
to purify:— Mid. to purify oneself by offerings, τοῖς θεοῖς to the gods, Eur.
G6617:
ἀφάλλομαι
I. to spring off or from, ἐκ νεώς Aesch.; ἀφήλατο jumped off, Ar.
II. to rebound, glance off, Anth.
G6618:
ἀφάπτω
to fasten from or upon, ἅμματα ἀφ. to tie knots on a string, Hdt.:—Pass. to be hung on, hang on, perf. part. ἀπαμμένος (ionic for ἀφημμένος), Hdt.; ἀφημμένος ἔκ τινος Theocr.
G6622:
ἀφηγέομαι
Dep.
I. to lead from a point, and so, generally, to lead the way, go first, οἱ ἀφηγούμενοι the van, Xen.
II. to tell or relate in full, explain, Hdt.: perf. in pass. sense, τὸ ἀπηγημένον what has been told, id.
G6623:
ἄφθορος
uncorrupt, of young persons, Anth.
G6624:
ἀφοβία [From ἄφοβος]
fearlessness, Plat.
G6625:
ἄφοβος
without fear:
1. fearless, intrepid, dauntless, Pind., Soph.:—adv. ‐βως, Xen.
2. causing no fear, free from fear, Aesch.
3. ἄφοβοι θῆρες beasts which no one fears, i. e. cattle, Soph.
G6626:
ἀφορία [ἄφορος]
a not bearing:
1. non-production, dearth, καρπῶν Xen.
2. barrenness, sterility of land: metaph., ἀφ. φρενῶν id.
G6629:
ἀφρονέω [ἄφρων]
to be silly, act foolishly, only in part., Il., Anth.
G6638:
ἀωρία [ἄωρος]
a wrong time: acc. as adv., ἀωρίαν ἥκειν to have come too late, Ar.; ἀωρίαι at an unseasonable time, so late, Luc.
G6639:
ἄωρος [ὥρα]
I. untimely, unseasonable, Lat. intempestivus, Aesch., Eur.:—c. gen., γήρως ἀωρότερα things unbecoming old age, Plut.
2. unripe, ἄωρος πρὸς γάμον id.
II. without youthful freshness, ugly, Xen., Plat.

ἄωρος [ἀείρω, cf. μετέωρος]
pendulous, waving about, of the πλεκτάναι or polypus-like legs of Scylla, Od.
G6642:
βαδίζω [βάδος, βαίνω]
1. to go slowly, to walk, Lat. ambulare, Hhymn., Xen.: to go, march, of horsemen, id.: to go by land, Dem.:—c. acc. cogn., βάδον, ὁδὸν β. Ar., Xen.
2. generally, ἐπ’ οἰκίας βαδ. to enter houses, Dem.: to proceed (in argument), id.:—of things, αἱ τιμαὶ ἐπ’ ἔλαττον ἐβάδιζον prices were getting lower, id.
G6647:
βαίνω [Root ΒΑ]
A. in most forms,
I. intr. to walk, step, properly of motion on foot, ποσσὶ or ποσὶ βαίνειν Hom., etc.; c. inf. in Hom., βῆ ἰέναι, βῆ ἰέμεν set out to go, went his way, Il.; βῆ θέειν started to run, id.; βῆ δ’ ἐλάαν, id., etc.:—c. acc. loci, Soph.; and with all Preps. implying motion, as, ἐπὶ νηὸς ἔβαινεν was going on board ship, Od.; ἐφ’ ἵππων βάντες having mounted the chariot, id.; βαίνειν δῑ αἵματος to wade through blood, Eur., etc.
2. in perf. to stand or be in a place, χῶρος ἐν ὧι βεβήκαμεν Soph.; often almost= εἰμί (sum), εὖ βεβηκώς on a good footing, well established, prosperous, Hdt., etc.; so, οἱ ἐν τέλει βεβῶτες they who are in office, id., Soph.; cf. ξυρόν.
3. to go, go away, depart, Il., Soph.; βέβηκα euphem. for τέθνηκα, Aesch., Soph.:—of things, ἐννέα ἐνιαυτοὶ βεβάασι nine years have come and gone, Il.
4. to come, τίπτε βέβηκας; id.: to arrive, Soph.
5. to go on, advance, ἐς τόδε τόλμης, ἐς τοσοῦτον ἐλπίδων id.
II. c. acc. to mount, Hom. only in aor1 mid., βήσασθαι δίφρον:— Pass., ἵπποι βαινόμεναι brood mares, Hdt.
2. χρέος ἔβα με debts came on me, Ar.
3. in Poets, with acc. of the instrument of motion, which is simply pleonastic, βαίνειν πόδα to advance the foot, step on, Eur., etc.
B. Causal, in fut. βήσω, aor1 ἔβησα:— to make to go, βῆσεν ἀφ’ ἵππον, ἐξ ἵππων βῆσε brought them down from the chariot, Il. The pres. in this sense is βιβάζω.
G6648:
βακτηρία [= βάκτρον,]
a staff, cane, Ar., Thuc.: borne as a badge of office by the δικασταί, Dem.
G6650:
βάλανος [deriv. uncertain]
I. an acorn, Lat. glans, the fruit of the φηγός, given to swine, Od.:— any similar fruit, the date, Hdt., Xen.
II. from similarity of shape, an iron peg, a bolt-pin, Lat. pessulus, passed through the wooden bar (μοχλός) into the door-post, so that the bar could not be removed till the pin was taken out with a hook (βαλανάγρα), Ar., Thuc.
G6651:
βάμμα [βάπτω]
that in which a thing is dipped, dye, Plat., v. βάπτω I. 3.
G6653:
βάραθρον [deriv. uncertain]
1. a gulf, pit:— at Athens a cleft behind the Acropolis, into which criminals were thrown, Hdt., Ar.
2. metaph. ruin, perdition, Dem.
G6654:
βᾶρις
a flat-bottomed boat, used in Egypt, Hdt., Aesch.
G6656:
βαρυθυμέω [from βαρύθυμος]
to be weighed down: to be heavy at heart: in Mid., Plut.
G6659:
βάσκανος [deriv. uncertain]
I. slanderous, envious, malignant, Ar., Dem.
II. as Subst. a slanderer, id.
2. a sorcerer, id.
G6660:
βάσταγμα [from βαστάζω]
that which is borne, a burden, Eur.
G6661:
βδέλλα [from βδάλλω]
a leech, Hdt., Theocr.
G6671:
βιβάζω
Causal of βαίνω, to make to mount, to lift up, exalt, Soph.
G6672:
βίβλινος
βίβλινος, οἶνος , Biblian wine, from Biblis in Thrace, Hes., Theocr.: βύβλινος in Eur.
G6675:
βῖκος
Oriental word for a wine-jar, Hdt., Xen.
G6678:
βλέφαρον [βλέπω] [γλέφαρον is variously listed as Doric and Aeolic.]
I. mostly in pl. the eyelids, Hom.
II. the eyes, Trag.: ἁμέρας βλέφαρον, νυκτὸς βλέφαρον, i. e. the sun, the moon, Soph., Eur.
G6679:
βόθρος [Prob. from the same Root as βαθύς: cp. also Lat. fodio.]
any hole or pit dug in the ground, Lat. puteus, Hom.: a natural trough for washing clothes in, Od.:— a hole, such as a fire makes in the snow, Xen.
G6680: βοίδιον [Dim. of βοῦς, Ar.]
G6682:
βόλος [βάλλω]
1. a throw with a casting-net, a cast, Orac. ap. Hdt., Theocr.: metaph., εἰς βόλον καθίστασθαι to fall within the cast of the net, Eur.
2. the thing caught, a draft of fish, Aesch., id.
G6683:
βομβέω [βόμβος]
to make a booming, humming noise, to sound deep or hollow, Hom.; βόμβησαν κατὰ ῥόον the oars fell with a loud noise down into the tide, Od.; βόμβησεν λίθος the stone flew humming through the air, id.:—of bees, to hum, Theocr.; of mosquitoes, to buzz, Ar.
G6684:
βορά [v. βιβρώσκω]
eatage, meat, properly of carnivorous beasts, Trag.; of cannibal-like feast, Hdt., Trag.:—rarely of simple food, Aesch., Soph.
G6685:
βόσκημα [βόσκω]
I. that which is fed or fatted: in pl. fatted beasts, cattle, Soph., etc.; of sheep, Eur.; of horses, id.; of pigs, Ar.
II. food, Aesch.
G6686:
βόστρυχος [βότρυς]
1. a curl or lock of hair, Aesch., etc.
2. anything twisted or wreathed, πυρὸς β., of a flash of lightning, id.
G6690:
βουκόλιον [From βουκόλος]
I. a herd of cattle, Hdt., Theocr.
II. a means of beguiling, Anth.
G6691:
βουλευτικός [βουλεύω]
I. of or for the council or the councillors, Xen., Dem.
2. able to advise or deliberate, Plat., etc.
II. as Subst., βουλευτικόν, in the Athen. theatre, the seats next the orchestra, reserved for the Council, Ar.
2. the senatorial order, Plut.
G6693:
βούτομον [τεμεῖν]
butomus, the flowering rush, Ar., Theocr.
G6697:
βρόμος [βρέμω]
1. Lat. fremitus, any loud noise, as the crackling of fire, Il.; roaring of a storm, Aesch.; neighing of horses, id.
2. rage, fury, Eur.
G6698:
βροντάω [from βροντή]
1. to thunder, Od.; metaph. of Pericles, Ar.
2. impers., βροντᾶι it thunders, id.
G6699:
βροτός [The orig. form seems to have been μορτός, cf. ἄμβροτος.]
a mortal man, Hom., attic Poets.
